method.claimBoundary: Readiness mapping only. No GLEIF or QVI qualification assessment, formal audit or GAAM conformance claim is made.

findings.title: Credential authority and transaction authority must remain distinct
findings.observation: vLEI artifacts can strongly establish organizational identity, role and credential-governance authority, but downstream transaction authority remains context dependent.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Require relying systems to evaluate effect-specific authority independently of credential validity or organizational role unless the credential semantics explicitly establish that authority.
candidateTests: valid role credential cannot authorize an unrelated transaction
transaction exceeding mandate is denied

establishes: organizational identity or role within declared credential semantics

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Authorization vLEI is a strong delegated-authority pattern
findings.observation: Authorization credentials and delegated identifiers provide explicit, cryptographically verifiable delegation for defined credential-governance actions.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Use the Authorization vLEI model as a GAAM reference case for testing delegation source, scope, acceptance, lineage and revocation requirements.
candidateTests: delegation lineage resolves to originating authority
inactive or revoked delegation is rejected
knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Role semantics can be broadened by downstream relying systems
findings.observation: Official Organizational Role and Engagement Context Role credentials are typed, but external verifiers may infer authority beyond the declared role semantics.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Publish positive and negative reliance semantics for each role credential class, including what the artifact does not by itself establish.
candidateTests: verifier cannot substitute role recognition for unrestricted mandate
engagement-context authority does not escape its context
knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Delegation lineage is strong but revocation propagation should be explicit
findings.observation: Technical delegation and credential status are strong, while different upstream state changes can have different downstream consequences.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Model parent-child dependency classes and propagation rules across qualification, delegated identifiers, authorization credentials and role credentials.
candidateTests: revoking parent authority invalidates declared descendants
replacement does not invalidate unrelated branches
multi-hop validity checks each active hop

doesNotEstablish: uniform downstream invalidation for every upstream event

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Trust assurance is strong but assurance scope must stay bounded
findings.observation: The Trust Assurance Framework maps requirements to governance, qualification, certification and software enforcement mechanisms that establish different forms of evidence.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Use vLEI as a reference case for explicit assurance composition: every assurance artifact should state what it establishes, its limitations and allowed dependencies.
candidateTests: one assurance form cannot satisfy an unrelated claim
composed assurance exposes each dependency and limitation
knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: The framework exposes assurance boundaries outside directly assessed actors
findings.observation: The assurance model acknowledges areas where compliance of ecosystem participants beyond directly assessed parties cannot be determined by the governing authority.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Adopt explicit assurance-state vocabulary for assessed, self-attested, externally assured, unobserved and unknown conditions rather than forcing binary trust state.
candidateTests: unobserved actor state cannot be reported as assessed
known monitoring gaps remain visible in composed assurance

doesNotEstablish: compliance of actors outside the assessor's practical perimeter

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Periodic qualification is not identical to continuous governance assurance
findings.observation: Annual qualification, status, incident and operational evidence provide strong recurring assurance inputs but do not by themselves define one event-driven governance assurance state.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Separate periodic reassessment from continuous controls and declare freshness, drift, trigger, escalation and suspension semantics for each monitored condition.
candidateTests: expired periodic evidence degrades assurance
material incident triggers reassessment
blind period is explicitly represented

doesNotEstablish: continuous governance assurance without explicit event-driven state

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Institutional governance authority is less machine-actionable than credential authority
findings.observation: Credential and identifier authority can be cryptographically resolved, while higher institutional authority remains primarily documentary and organizational.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Require resolvable provenance from technical authority through ecosystem governance to institutional authority without requiring constitutional governance to become executable code.
candidateTests: technical authority resolves to a current governance source
superseded governance source cannot silently remain authoritative
knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Reliance semantics can be made more explicit
findings.observation: A verifier can establish validity, provenance, role and qualification while still needing policy to determine what conclusions or effects are justified.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Define machine-readable establishes and does-not-establish semantics for each governed artifact and relationship class.
candidateTests: credential validity cannot satisfy a claim class outside declared semantics
accreditation or qualification cannot guarantee every downstream output

establishes: validity, provenance, role or qualification as declared
doesNotEstablish: claims or effects outside declared semantics

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Challenge exists but downstream remedy is less operationalized
findings.observation: Challenge and correction mechanisms can address incorrect trust data, while remedy for effects already caused by downstream reliance is a separate governance problem.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Represent correction and remedy as distinct lifecycle stages and record when downstream effects require additional action after a credential or record is corrected.
candidateTests: successful challenge changes future reliance state
past consequential effects remain flagged for remedy where applicable

doesNotEstablish: automatic remedy of effects already produced

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Downstream accountability spans issuer and relying-system boundaries
findings.observation: vLEI can establish authoritative facts while the final consequential decision may be made by an external relying application under separate governance.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Define explicit issuer, holder and relying-party accountability boundaries so valid evidence cannot displace responsibility for an overbroad downstream decision.
candidateTests: valid credential plus invalid relying policy produces a relying-party failure
issuer accountability is not expanded beyond the credential's supported claim

doesNotEstablish: transfer of final decision accountability to the credential issuer

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.

findings.title: vLEI is suitable for a machine-actionable GAAM reference crosswalk
findings.observation: The ecosystem already exposes structured governance documents, roles, credential schemas, delegation, lifecycle and assurance evidence suitable for reproducible mapping.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Use vLEI as a benchmark for validating GAAM crosswalk methodology against an ecosystem with substantial existing executable governance.
candidateTests: every crosswalk requirement resolves to source and evidence expectation
crosswalk distinguishes source coverage from observed implementation behaviour

doesNotEstablish: formal GAAM conformance or GLEIF assessment
